correctness.rationale: The unit-edge facet areas and Cauchy's formula give three axis terms of weight one and four body-diagonal terms of weight 3 sqrt(3)/2. After sorting absolute coordinates only the diagonal form -a+b+c can change sign, giving both branches. For the minimum, use the rays (1,1,0), (1,1,1), (2,1,1) in the first cone and (1,0,0), (1,1,0), (2,1,1) in the other. The triangle inequality extends the least ray ratio to each cone; the unique least ray in each is (1,1,0). The linear maximum in the second cone is attained in its interior at the normalized gradient (7,1,1), and exceeds the first cone's bound 4 sqrt(3). The two orbits have sizes 12 and 24. Gaussian radial separation divides the bivariate normal absolute-product moment by 3, and axis/axis, diagonal/diagonal and mixed unordered pairs have counts 3, 6, 12, giving the claimed second moment. Independent bounded arithmetic gives variance 0.093312449145, consistent with the formula.
residual_risks: The bounded arithmetic is not a certificate of an all-directions or integration theorem; those follow from the proof. No formal verification claimed.
